title: Denormalize a star into a wide reporting table
objective_text: Flatten a fact table and its dimensions into one wide table with one row per fact, keeping every fact even when a dimension row is missing.
scenario: A data science team wants the sales star as one flat table they can load into a notebook without joins. The fact has a sale whose product key was never matched, and the team must still see it, labelled Unknown, or their totals won't match finance's.
verifies: Your SQL ran on this PC with DuckDB and gold_sales_wide has one row per sale with the expected attributes and totals.
does_not_verify: How a wide table performs in Direct Lake or a Fabric Warehouse compared with the star: that depends on the service.
That the SQL runs unchanged in Spark SQL or T-SQL.

expected.result: The starter's final SELECT over gold_sales_wide, ordered by sale_id.

validation.pass: Every sale is there with its attributes.
validation.fail: Count the rows of fact_sales and of your table, then check the sale with product_key 99.

validation.pass: One row per sale and no blank attributes.
validation.fail: A sale appears twice or an attribute is blank.

hints: Start from fact_sales and LEFT JOIN each dimension, so no sale is lost.
coalesce(p.product_name, 'Unknown') labels the sale whose product isn't in dim_product.
explanation: Denormalizing copies dimension attributes onto every fact row. Start from the fact and left join outward so the row count never changes; label missing members instead of dropping them; and check the result's row count and totals against the fact. A wide table is convenient for notebooks and some reports, but it repeats attributes and must be rebuilt when a dimension changes.
reset: Reset restores the star and drops gold_sales_wide.
